The funny thing is, I have no idea where that phrase came from. I've done some google searches, and almost every result I find is equally likely on the "That's where I got the idea" list.

My personal opinion is that Character-Bibs didn't really 'go Green Lantern', because Author-Bibs is so self-deprecating that he wouldn't believe that he deserved to be one. He'd just be a pud with kinda-almost-sorta Power Rings that kinda-sorta worked the way he wanted to.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
My brain is spinning in five different directions, trying to make sense of that statement.

About the story: Best. Self-insert fic. Ever. As soon as I read the part about Green Able and 682 turning yellow, I knew that Character-Bibs had gone Green Lantern on us. So, 682 will someday be neutralized by one of the SCP Cliches ("lol superhero") and 423 is an O5. Wow. *brain explodes*

…the quiet sound of a paradigm shifting without a clutch.

Where have I heard this line before…

Edit @ below post: Now I remember. "Paradigm shifting without a clutch" was a line from a Dilbert strip a few years back. Dogbert killed an Accounting Troll by wearing a hat backwards, and the line was his explanation for "that popping sound".

item.content:encoded:
So, I'm going to post a commentary on this one. I've broken it up into three sections, each one with a general thoughts about each 'block' of text.

For ease of explaining it, here's the terms I'm going to use:

Author-Bibs: The in-character Agent Bibs that wrote the original self-insert fanfic.
Character-Bibs: The Agent Bibs inside the story, written by Author-Bibs.

First 'Today' Section
Hide Section One

I conceptualized the Good Things Character-Bibs Did as things that Author-Bibs asked the higher-ups in the Foundation to test, but wasn't allowed permission to do so. So instead of whining, he added all the beefs he had into the story. Only while Author-Bibs didn't get permission, Character-Bibs did. I do like to think that Author-Bibs still wets himself when Abel startles him, though.

Its funny how hard it was to write this section, because I was generally going for full-on (to quote Fat Ghost) "BIBS IS GREAT YAY BIBS"

In my own head, I treat the idea that Author-Bibs is afraid of everything the rest of the Foundation isn't afraid of completely straight. I see Author-Bibs as a thought-based Macguyver.

The 'Two Weeks Earlier' Section
Hide Section Two

I tried to play this as 'realism with a heaping load of exageration'. I see Author-Bibs occasionally being left alone when it technically was against the rules to do so, if only because he's profoundly annoying a lot of the time. But since Author-Bibs knew that Character-Bibs wouldn't be left alone for such a test with 914, Author-Bibs wrote the staff as somewhat incompetant, wandering away like they did. I see this as 50% plot-oriented, and 50% dig at all the times Author-Bibs wanted the guards to go away.

I'll talk about it more in the third section, but it's intentional that I didn't come out and say what Character-Bibs refined.

Second 'Today' Section
Hide Section Three

So yeah, basically, Character-Bibs refined his plastic Lantern Power Rings into working Power Rings. He made a Green (Willpower) Power Ring and a Blue (Hope) Power Ring. Like in the comics, the creation of two Power Rings caused the other ones to come into fruition. One of them was the Red Lantern Ring of Rage, and what better owner for that one than 682?

I intentionally didn't come out and admit what they were. Author-Bibs wouldn't do it, because he wrote the story just for himself. He didn't need to say what they were, because he knew. Plus, there's a facet of arrogance to it: he wouldn't want people to know what he was talking about, if they did see it. He liked the idea that only he, and other major nerds, would get it.

Character-Bibs used a Green Ring to try and pry the Red Ring off 682. In the comics, Green typically has a weakness to Yellow. So Character-Bibs used his Blue Ring to counter the yellowing. Green+Blue kills Red/Yellow, leading to 682's death.

The ending, I hope, is obvious. Fred doesn't realize, until its too late, that Character-Bibs is still an Agent, so he knows that someone named Fred that he's never met is going to be SCP-423.

So yeah, a lot of text for a stupid story, but thats what I do. Feel free to comment.
